title: Optional exercise: link objects into a chain
intro: Apply objects and pointer links after studying dynamic memory. This is an optional extension, not a separate core lesson.
question: Does a next pointer own or automatically construct the Node it points to?
answer: No. A pointer stores an address. In this exercise the nodes are local objects, so their lifetimes are controlled by their scopes. Do not delete them.

exercise.task: Connect a(10), b(20), and c(30) into a chain ending in nullptr. Implement printChain and countNodes, including an empty chain. Then insert extra(15) after a while preserving b and c.
exercise.hint: Walk a const Node* until nullptr. For insertion, set extra.next to the old a.next before changing a.next to &extra.
exercise.explanation: The counts are 3, 0, and 4. The chains print 10 20 30 and then 10 15 20 30. Reversing the insertion assignments can create a self-loop or lose the remaining chain.
